To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: FY28 staged targets & contingency playbook — QBR prep

Team,

Kicking off FY28 planning. Goal: align leadership on a set of staged targets (base / stretch / conservative) and a short contingency playbook to use during the QBR window. I want us to come to the first leadership sync with:

- an initial set of revenue and ARR targets by product line (base/stretch)
- 3 downside scenarios with trigger points and immediate actions
- a draft QBR playbook (audience, key metrics, escalations)

Proposed timeline:
- Feb 20–24: internal drafts and assumptions
- Feb 25: leadership pre-read distributed
- Mar 1: Leadership QBR rehearsal + finalize playbook

Marissa: can you surface the FY27 run-rate and key variance drivers by EOD Monday? Laura: please validate sales capacity assumptions. Karthik/Markus: ops and engineering capacity and hiring constraints — flag any hard ceilings.

Attachments: FY28_assumptions_v1.xlsx (work-in-progress)

I'll schedule a 60-min sync for Monday to walk the initial assumptions. Thanks — this is high priority for exec QBR.

— Vivek
VP, GTM Strategy

Vivek — quick clarifying Qs before Monday's sync:

1) Base vs stretch: do we want ARR knife-edge or revenue-based? My suggestion is to set ARR as the north star and revenue for short-term channel pushes.
2) For downside triggers, can we define SLOs for customer churn and deal slippage as % of ARR (e.g., 2% churn month-over-month)?
3) I'll need the deal-level pipeline export — can Marissa share a filtered export (closed-won last 12 months, churn flags) so Sales Capacity model aligns.

Also, suggest a 40-slide max pre-read; teams hate huge docs. I'll start a 1-page summary for leadership.

Thanks,
Laura
Director, Finance
Redwood Inference

Vivek/Team — attached the first-pass exports you asked for. Notes below: 

Attachments included: FY28_assumptions_v1.xlsx (tabs: ARR_trace, variance_drivers, pipeline_sample), resource_headcount_model.csv (current hiring plan), QBR_playbook_draft.docx (template).

Key callouts from the data export:
- FY27 run-rate shows a 12% uplift in net new ARR vs plan, but 4 large deals accounted for 55% of incremental ARR.
- Churn: gross churn concentrated in the self-serve segment; enterprise churn low but renewal timelines slipped in Q4.
- Pipeline health: weighted pipeline coverage at 2.1x for base target; coverage drops to 1.3x for stretch.

I added two proposed downside scenarios in the assumptions tab: (A) macro pullback — reduce closed rate by 30%; (B) product SLA incident — 3% ARR at risk due to retention shock. Each has suggested mitigations in the playbook doc (pricing credits, focused AE activity, temporary prioritization of reliability fixes).

I'll be on the sync Monday and can walk the ARR tab.

Vivek/Team — quick ops perspective: 

- Hiring ceilings: we have two critical blockers for ramp in H1: (1) infra SRE hiring is behind plan (20% behind), (2) senior latency/serving eng hires have 3–4 month lead times. That creates a hard ceiling on feature throughput and potentially delays prioritized reliability work.
- Cost levers: we can pause non-essential infra spend and extend experiment windows to free headcount for reliability work — will quantify impact for Monday.
- Timing: to be useful for QBR, we need the leadership pre-read out by Feb 25 COB so we can iterate with the CEO's office.

Action: Markus — please confirm if the current hiring plan in resource_headcount_model.csv is accurate; I can mark which roles can be delayed with minimal product impact.

Thanks,
Karthik

- Marissa: I'll review the ARR tabs tonight. Please surface the filtered pipeline export Laura requested by 09:00 Mon.
- Laura: draft the 1-page leadership summary (ARR north star, top 3 risks, ask of leadership) — drop in the Drive folder by COB Monday.

Sync details: Monday Feb 23, 10:00–11:00 PT (calendar invite to follow). Goal for the meeting: agree on base/stretch targets and finalize the QBR playbook outline for CEO review.

I'll also loop Finance (external consultant) for one quick sanity check on downside scenarios Friday morning — Olivia from Olive Finance and Ben from FinOps Consulting will be on a 30-min call to sanity-check assumptions.

If anything materially changes, flag in this thread.
